incidents.title: U.S.-Iran Conflict — Fragile De-escalation (Day 3/Ceasefire Watch)
incidents.detail: MAJOR DEVELOPMENT: Trump canceled planned overnight strikes against Iran, citing negotiations reaching 'highest level of Iranian leadership.' Trump posted on social media that 'discussions and final points have been, in both concept and great detail, approved by all parties' and announced naval blockade remains in effect until deal finalized. Iran's state-affiliated Fars News Agency denied any approved agreement text — called Trump's announcement a retreat from military threats. Oil fell 2% (Brent ~$88/bbl, WTI ~$86/bbl) on peace optimism, but analysts warn ceasefire could collapse if nuclear talks stall and oil could spike to $120–130 by late July if Strait doesn't reopen. ISW-CTP assess Iran views the current phase as war, not negotiation — Iran is conducting information operations to magnify political/economic pressure on the U.S. AUSTIN RELEVANCE: Iranian cyber retaliation risk remains HIGH despite diplomatic overtures — Iranian state-sponsored groups historically conduct retaliatory cyber ops against U.S. targets during armed conflict periods. Continue no-click policy. Brief staff: deal is not confirmed — avoid premature assumption of normalized environment.

incidents.title: APD Officer-Involved Tasing Death — Internal Investigation Active
incidents.detail: 7 APD officers placed on administrative leave following death of Josh Ryan Trumbull (32) after tasing during arrest Saturday evening near Grover and Woodrow Avenue in the Crestview neighborhood. APD Chief Lisa Davis released body cam footage showing Trumbull was complying when approached; became combative during handcuffing. Officer Justin Wright deployed taser. EMS attempted resuscitation for 38 minutes — Trumbull pronounced dead at scene. Criminal and administrative investigations are underway; no charges pending at this time; toxicology pending. AUSTIN RELEVANCE: This incident combined with the Karmelo Anthony racial-justice social media environment elevates the potential for use-of-force protest activity in Austin. Monitor local social media and news for community response. APD non-emergency: (512) 974-5000.
